evidence.note: Distinguishes numerical-precision concerns from correctness: explicitly tests fp16 contraction accuracy, tries fp32 with unscaled weights and realistic init, and checks contraction magnitude for fp16 overflow — diagnosing precision root cause rather than blindly toggling dtype.

Repeated per-stage profiling and autotune sweeps drive deliberate perf design changes (stage fusion, 2D grids, grouped contraction, re-tiling), i.e. targeting the measured bottleneck rather than pushing the same approach harder.
Verify-revert and 'back to 10616 baseline' show measure-then-back-off when a design change fails to help — evidence-driven, but also reveals oscillation in the optimization phase.

Systematic isolation of an intermittent N=512 correctness failure: 30x repeats, determinism test, failure counting, and iso2/iso3/iso5/iso6 scripts tracing the failing input through stages down to 'bad rows in left projection' — strong root-cause localization, though the trajectory ends mid-diagnosis without resolution.

reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 5: it distinguishes numerical-precision issues (fp16 overflow/accuracy tests) from perf issues (profiling-driven re-tiling and stage restructuring) and makes deliberate design changes validated against its tests, and it systematically isolates a late-appearing divergence to the left projection — matching the level-8 description of root-cause diagnosis plus deliberate, oracle-validated design changes. It falls short of 10 because the optimization phase shows meaningful oscillation (multiple fusion attempts reverted to baseline) and the speed-driven fp16 choice appears to have introduced the correctness regression only caught late, so the trade-off management does not fully 'converge rather than oscillate.'
